# llm-production-engineering

> Field notes from building AI systems in production since 2019. The ops side of LLM serving: cost tracking, eval-driven deployment, capacity planning, observability, incident playbooks, and decision frameworks.
> Source: https://github.com/sailikhithk/llm-production-engineering

Most LLM inference content explains how the systems work: PagedAttention internals, quantization algorithms, attention variants. This repo covers the other half: how to run them in production. Track cost per token, catch quality drift before users do, plan capacity, survive preemption storms, and pick the right engine for your workload.

## Sections

- [01-cost-tracking](docs/01-cost-tracking/): Per-token cost attribution, budget enforcement, chargeback
- [02-eval-driven-deployment](docs/02-eval-driven-deployment/): Quality drift detection, golden-set regression, canary deploys
- [03-capacity-planning](docs/03-capacity-planning/): Sizing LLM serving, autoscaling, GPU allocation math
- [04-observability](docs/04-observability/): TTFT, ITL, SLOs, OTel signals for LLM serving
- [05-incident-playbooks](docs/05-incident-playbooks/): Preemption storms, GPU failure, KV cache pressure, cold start spikes
- [06-decision-framework](docs/06-decision-framework/): Engine, quantization, and config selection decision trees
- [07-engine-tradeoffs](docs/07-engine-tradeoffs/): vLLM vs SGLang vs TensorRT-LLM vs llama.cpp production matrix

## Reference code

- [code/cost_tracker/](code/cost_tracker/): OpenTelemetry-based per-token cost tracking reference impl
- [code/eval_harness/](code/eval_harness/): Golden-set regression harness for LLM quality drift
- [code/capacity_calculator/](code/capacity_calculator/): LLM serving sizing script (GPU count, KV cache budget)

## Why this repo exists

The gap this repo fills: there is plenty of content explaining how PagedAttention works or how AWQ quantizes weights, but almost nothing explaining how to track cost per token across 30+ models, catch quality drift before users complain, size GPU capacity for 100x traffic variance, handle vLLM preemption storms at 3am, or decide between vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM. Every recommendation comes from running these systems under real traffic.
